messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Access and use.** “The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel named in writing and approved by the designer before access. Each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as these terms. The testing house remains responsible for compliance. The same requirements apply to external specialists and replacement personnel. Neither the testing house nor anyone receiving access may use the drawings, geometry or materials derived from them to develop a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The testing house may make the minimum working copies needed for the tests. Digital copies and fixture files must be encrypted in transit and at rest and accessible only to approved personnel. The testing house may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate test fixtures and may use those fixtures only for the agreed tests. Physical fixtures must be secured against unauthorized access.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the designer accepts the test results in writing, or after earlier termination of the testing engagement, the testing house must return or securely destroy the supplied drawings and CAD files, securely delete all working copies and derivative files, and destroy all fixtures incorporating the supplied geometry. By the same deadline it must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier confirming completion and identifying the materials covered and the verification method. The verifier may inspect deletion records and witness fixture destruction. Access to CAD geometry requires the designer’s prior written approval. This certification replaces on-demand site audits.”

Can your lab certify deletion from backups within that window? If your quality system requires longer retention, please identify the records and retention period. We can agree to retention of test reports and measurement data that do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry.

Counterproposal. We can certify deletion from backups within 30 days only for geometry-bearing materials held in a dedicated encrypted Project Vault configured for immediate purge and a maximum 30-day backup retention. Our standard enterprise backup rotation is 90 days, so we will not certify enterprise backups for this engagement. All drawings, native CAD, extracts, derivative files and fixture files will be held only in that vault. Longer retention is limited to non-geometry records: calibration records and measurement traceability records for 2 years from calibration; test reports, raw measurement data and environmental logs for 2 years unless accreditation requires longer. Attachment E will list these, and retained records will be redacted and segregated so no drawing, CAD geometry or reconstruction information is disclosed.

Replacement wording:

**Access and use.** “The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to the organizations and individuals listed in Attachment A. Each organization and individual must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as these terms before access. The testing house remains fully responsible and must flow these terms down to every external specialist, including the machining shop and accredited lab listed in Attachment A. Neither the testing house nor any recipient may use the drawings, CAD geometry, extracts or materials derived from them to develop a competing product.

Substitution: a new external organization requires the designer’s prior written approval, not to be unreasonably withheld. Within an already approved organization, the testing house may substitute an individual without prior approval by giving written notice at least two business days before access, provided the substitute is bound by equivalent written obligations; the designer may require removal of that individual within five business days on documented security grounds. Native CAD may be accessed only in the Project Vault by named approved personnel. Any access to CAD geometry beyond the supplied materials requires the designer’s prior written approval.”

**Working copies, extracts and fixtures.** “The testing house may make the minimum working copies needed for the tests. It may create only the Fixture Geometry Extracts listed in Attachment C, containing only the interface dimensions and features needed to design and fabricate fixtures. Extracts must not include native CAD, full geometry, hidden features, mass properties or sufficient information to reconstruct the actuator. Digital copies, extracts and fixture files must be encrypted in transit and at rest, stored only in the Project Vault, accessible only to approved personnel, with access logging. Backups of geometry-bearing data must be purged no later than the same 30-day deadline; the vault must support immediate purge and have maximum backup retention of 30 days. Physical fixtures must be stored in an access-controlled area, marked confidential, and used only for the agreed tests.”

**Destruction, retention and verification.** “Within 30 days after the designer accepts the test results in writing, or after earlier termination, the testing house must return or securely destroy the supplied drawings and CAD files, securely delete all working copies, extracts, derivative files and fixture files from active systems and Project Vault backups within the same 30-day window, and destroy all fixtures incorporating the supplied geometry. By the same deadline it must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier listed in Attachment F confirming completion, identifying the materials covered and the verification method. The verifier may review deletion logs, access logs, backup purge reports and redaction of retained records, and may witness fixture destruction by live remote session or at a scheduled appointment at the testing house’s facility. No unannounced inspections are permitted. Any on-site verification at a shared customer site requires at least ten business days’ notice and the site operator’s consent; otherwise verification is remote or at the testing house’s facility. This certification and scheduled verification replace on-demand site audits and unannounced inspections.

Retention carve-out: the testing house may retain records required by its quality system or accreditation that contain no drawings, CAD geometry, extracts, derivative geometry or information permitting reconstruction. Attachment E lists: calibration records and measurement traceability, 2 years; test reports, raw measurement data and environmental logs, 2 years unless accreditation requires longer; quality and nonconformance records as required. These records will be segregated, redacted and access-limited to quality, accreditation and regulatory purposes.”

**Attachments we propose:**

- **Attachment A** — approved organizations and personnel, including the accredited lab and machining shop; substitution mechanics as above.
- **Attachment B** — test scope, deliverables and written acceptance.
- **Attachment C** — approved Fixture Geometry Extracts, feature-level only; no native CAD or full geometry.
- **Attachment D** — security controls: Project Vault, encryption in transit and at rest, access logging, 30-day backup purge for geometry-bearing data, approved storage locations.
- **Attachment E** — retention schedule as above, with redaction standard.
- **Attachment F** — verification: approved independent verifiers, records to be reviewed, remote/scheduled witness process, no unannounced inspections, ten business days’ notice for any shared-site visit.

We can accept the dedicated Project Vault, the Attachment C limits on fixture extracts, and independent certification by the 30-day deadline. Remote verification is acceptable, as are the proposed notice and consent terms for a shared-site visit. We propose three edits to close the remaining points.

**Personnel substitutions.** “Before an individual receives access, the designer must approve that individual by name in Attachment A or by email identifying the individual, organization, role and materials covered. The designer will respond to substitution requests within two business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval. The parties may list named alternates in Attachment A. The testing house may activate an approved alternate by written notice once equivalent written obligations are in place. It must revoke the outgoing individual’s access when the substitution takes effect.” This lets the lab cover a shift immediately with a named alternate.

**Machining and backup scope.** “The Project Vault restriction applies at every recipient, including the machining shop and accredited lab. Geometry-bearing files, including machine programs containing fixture geometry, must remain in the vault and be excluded from enterprise backups. Any step requiring a local copy requires the designer’s prior written approval of the file, device, personnel and purge procedure in Attachment D. The independent certificate must cover all recipients, approved devices, vault backups and physical fixtures.” Can the shop machine directly from the vault, or does its controller need a local copy? If it needs one, please identify the minimum file and how the verifier can confirm deletion.

**Retained records.** “Attachment E must identify each retained record class, its retention period and the event that starts that period. For any period required by accreditation, including for quality or nonconformance records, Attachment E must identify the applicable requirement. Retained records, considered together, must contain no geometry or information permitting reconstruction of the actuator. The independent verifier must confirm that the retained records meet this condition.”

With those edits, we can accept the balance of your wording. Attachments A through F should be agreed in writing before drawings or CAD are released.

Accepted on the Vault, Attachment C limits, 30-day independent certification, remote verification, and the shared-site notice/consent terms. Here is our answer to the machining question and replacement wording for the three open points.

**Machining question.** The machining shop's CNC controller cannot execute directly from the Project Vault; it requires a local machine program at the controller. We propose two permitted methods, in order of preference:

1. **Network DNC streaming** from the Vault to the controller, with the controller configured to disable disk spooling and caching. The Vault access log and controller log then evidence that no local file was retained. The verifier confirms via Vault access logs, controller log extract, and a witnessed controller file-system listing.
2. **Local copy fallback**, only with the designer's prior written approval of the file, device, personnel and purge procedure in Attachment D. Minimum file set: (i) the posted NC/machine program for the fixture only, and (ii) the setup sheet containing only the Attachment C interface dimensions. No native CAD, no extract files, no fixture models, no design geometry. Transfer by encrypted media or one-time encrypted download to an isolated, non-networked controller. Purge: delete the local file, clear spool/recycle, run a wipe, record the file hash at transfer and confirm absence after purge, with the shop supervisor signing the purge log. The verifier confirms deletion via the hash manifest, signed purge log, witnessed controller file-system listing, media destruction certificate, and Vault access logs showing no other transfers. Machine programs containing fixture geometry are geometry-bearing: they stay out of enterprise backups at every recipient, are covered by the destruction certificate, and are listed by hash in Attachment D.

**Replacement wording — personnel and substitutions.** "Access is limited to the organizations in Attachment A and to individuals named in Attachment A or approved by the designer by email identifying the individual, organization, role and materials covered; the designer will respond within two business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval. Attachment A will name at least one alternate for each critical role; the testing house may activate an approved alternate by written notice once equivalent written obligations are in place, and must revoke the outgoing individual's access when the substitution takes effect. Urgent substitution: where a scheduled test cannot proceed and no approved alternate is available, the testing house may grant temporary access for up to two business days to an individual of an approved organization who is already bound by that organization's written confidentiality and use obligations at least as protective as these terms, provided written notice is given to the designer within four business hours of access and the designer may require removal of that individual within five business days on documented security grounds. All substitutions and temporary accesses will be recorded in the access log and listed in the verification certificate."

Tradeoff we are accepting: name-level approval by the designer is retained, but we keep the named-alternate and short-notice urgent path so a specialist can be substituted mid-job without stopping the test. The designer keeps a documented-grounds removal right and full logging.

**Replacement wording — machining, devices and backup scope.** "The Project Vault restriction applies at every recipient, including the machining shop and accredited lab. Geometry-bearing files, including machine programs containing fixture geometry, must remain in the Vault and be excluded from enterprise backups. Machining shall be performed by DNC streaming with no local retention where the controller supports it; any required local copy needs the designer's prior written approval of the file, device, personnel and purge procedure in Attachment D, limited to the minimum file set described there. The independent certificate must cover all recipients, approved devices and media, Vault backups, local copies and purge evidence, physical fixtures, and all personnel substitutions and temporary accesses."

**Replacement wording — Attachment E (retained records).** Attachment E will list each class with its retention period, trigger event and governing requirement:

| Record class | Retention | Trigger | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibration records and measurement traceability (certificates, as-found/as-left data, equipment list, uncertainty data) | 2 years | Date of each calibration | Lab QMS implementing ISO/IEC 17025:2017 cl. 6.4 and 8.4 |
| Test reports, raw measurement data, environmental logs for the actuator vibration tests | 2 years | Issue date of the final test report | Lab QMS implementing ISO/IEC 17025:2017 cl. 7.8 and 8.4 |
| Nonconformance and corrective-action records | 2 years minimum; longer only where our accreditation scope or an applicable requirement sets a longer period, cited record-by-record in Attachment E | Date of closure | ISO/IEC 17025:2017 cl. 8.4 and the cited accreditation requirement |
| Access logs, purge logs, destruction and verification records | 2 years | Date of the verification certificate | Lab QMS; provided to the verifier |

Retained records, considered together, will contain no drawings, CAD, extracts, derivative geometry or information permitting reconstruction of the actuator: test reports will carry test conditions, results, instrument IDs and dates only; any dimension is redacted unless the verifier is satisfied it cannot permit reconstruction. The independent verifier will confirm this condition by reviewing the redaction standard and sampling the retained records under confidentiality, and the certificate will state that confirmation.

We accept that Attachments A through F are agreed in writing before any drawings or CAD are released, and that the certificate replaces on-demand audits with no unannounced inspections; any shared-site visit remains subject to ten business days' notice and site-operator consent per Attachment F.

We accept the machining and verification terms, including DNC streaming without local retention and the fallback requiring prior written approval in Attachment D. We also accept the Attachment E schedule and the verifier’s review of retained records. We have one remaining edit.

Please replace the urgent-substitution sentence with the following wording.

> If a scheduled test would otherwise stop and no approved alternate is available, the testing house may request expedited approval by email, naming the individual, approved organization, role, materials needed and requested access period. The designer may designate an on-call approver in Attachment A. An email approval takes effect immediately. The testing house may grant access once it has received that approval and confirmed equivalent written confidentiality and use obligations. Access is limited to the approved materials and expires when the assignment ends or after two business days, whichever comes first, unless the designer approves an extension in writing.

The named-alternate provision gives the lab an immediate route for shift coverage. The expedited route covers an unexpected specialist while preserving approval by name before disclosure. We can agree to the full wording with this substitution and with Attachments A through F agreed in writing before release.

Accepted. Your expedited-approval wording preserves approval by name before any disclosure, which is the point we needed to hold, while still letting us substitute a specialist mid-job. Here is the consolidated final clause with your sentence substituted for our urgent-access sentence:

**Access, use and substitutions.** "The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to the organizations listed in Attachment A and to individuals named in Attachment A or approved by the designer by email identifying the individual, organization, role and materials covered; the designer will respond within two business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval. Attachment A will name at least one alternate for each critical role; the testing house may activate an approved alternate by written notice once equivalent written obligations are in place, and must revoke the outgoing individual's access when the substitution takes effect. If a scheduled test would otherwise stop and no approved alternate is available, the testing house may request expedited approval by email, naming the individual, approved organization, role, materials needed and requested access period. The designer may designate an on-call approver in Attachment A. An email approval takes effect immediately. The testing house may grant access once it has received that approval and confirmed equivalent written confidentiality and use obligations. Access is limited to the approved materials and expires when the assignment ends or after two business days, whichever comes first, unless the designer approves an extension in writing. The designer may require removal of any individual within five business days on documented security grounds. Each organization and individual must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as these terms before access, and the testing house remains fully responsible and must flow these terms down to every external specialist, including the machining shop and accredited lab listed in Attachment A. Neither the testing house nor any recipient may use the drawings, CAD geometry, extracts or materials derived from them to develop a competing product. All substitutions, activations and temporary approvals will be recorded in the access log and listed in the verification certificate. Native CAD may be accessed only in the Project Vault by named approved personnel; any access to CAD geometry beyond the supplied materials requires the designer's prior written approval."

With that substitution, we agree the full wording as exchanged: Project Vault with 30-day backup purge for geometry-bearing data; Attachment C feature-level fixture extracts only; DNC streaming without local retention, with the Attachment D approved fallback limited to the minimum machine-program and setup-sheet file set, hash manifest and signed purge log; destruction and independent certification within 30 days of written acceptance or termination, covering all recipients, devices, media, vault backups, local copies, purge evidence, fixtures and personnel substitutions; remote verification with no unannounced inspections and ten business days' notice plus site-operator consent for any shared-site visit; and the Attachment E retention schedule with verifier confirmation that retained records contain no geometry or reconstruction information.

Attachments A through F will be agreed and signed in writing before any drawings or CAD are released. Attachment A will include the on-call approver designation, named alternates per critical role, and the approved organizations. Attachment D will include the minimum local-copy file set, device and purge procedure. Attachment F will list the approved independent verifiers and the remote-witness process.

We consider the terms resolved on this basis.
